Need to search first.I wasn't able to research Isaiah 38 this time, so I have no notes to give you.

**What went wrong:**
- **The page fetches failed.** I tried to open the verse-by-verse pages directly (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary and Barnes on biblehub.com, and preceptaustin.org). Every request was refused because the tool only opens addresses that have first come up in a search.
- **The searches failed too.** My first batch of searches went over the tool's usage limit. When I tried again, my code had a bug and crashed before it showed any results. Before I could fix it, I ran out of tool calls for this turn.

So I didn't read a single page. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Notes written now would be from memory, so I haven't written any.

**Next steps:** if you ask me to try again, I'll run the searches first and then open the pages they turn up. I'll do it a few searches at a time to stay under the limit. My plan:
1. **The traditional reading:** the Enduring Word page for Isaiah 38, then the Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit and Barnes commentaries on biblehub.com or studylight.org, and the preceptaustin.org page for Isaiah 38.
2. **Where traditions differ:**
   - Whether Hezekiah's prayer changed what God planned (vv. 1–5), from Reformed teachers (Ligonier, Desiring God) and from Wesleyan and Pentecostal ones (seedbed.com, wesley.nnu.edu, enduringword.com).
   - How v. 18 fits with life after death, from gotquestions.org and Lutheran sites.
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible notes on the "stairway of Ahaz" (v. 8) and on the hard Hebrew in vv. 12–16.
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings of Hezekiah's song (vv. 9–20), which is sung in church services, from newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org.
   - What the sites say about the fig poultice (v. 21) and the debate over medicine versus faith healing, which bears on word-of-faith teaching.

Let me know if you'd like me to go ahead.
